counterfactual_missing_items: No persistent ST-segment elevation in contiguous leads diagnostic of STEMI
No evidence of prior infarction or chronic ischemic changes beyond acute event
No findings supporting hypertensive heart disease as primary (e.g., left ventricular hypertrophy)
decisive_items: Upsloping ST-segment depression leads V1 through V6
Initial serum troponin I level: 1.159 ng/mL (normal range ≤0.028 ng/mL)
95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery
response.rationale: R5 is the most specific and complete diagnosis: elevated troponin with ST-segment depression and biphasic T waves without ST elevation defines NSTEMI, supported by LAD stenosis and anterior hypomotility. R6 is a broader syndrome category that includes NSTEMI but lacks specificity. R2 is accurate but under-specified, R3 contradicts the ECG pattern (no qualifying ST elevation), R1 and R7 are too broad or etiologically mismatched.

rejected.why: ECG shows ST-segment depression and only aVR elevation, not diagnostic STEMI criteria; contradicts STEMI.
Coronary artery disease is a chronic structural diagnosis, not the acute syndrome supported by troponin and ECG changes.
Hypertension history and BP do not explain acute troponin elevation, ECG changes, or LAD stenosis as the primary acute event.
